messages.author: 4fc24b6f8e2b4ec1
messages.subject: Hypothesis testing under CIM
parts:
Hello. Does anyone have a good suggestion on how to test the
contribution of individual QTLs under CIM? I the followoing situation:
tmp <- cim(data.scan,pheno.col=j,n.marcovar=5)
Would you test at each position using the number of markers as
cofactors you choose? In other words, would test H1 = model droping
each position (or putative QTL) in the genome vs. H0 = model fitting
using the 5 cofactors + QTL at position being tested? I think this
would be equivalent to the multiple QTL test shown in p 260 of Karl's
book. If this thinking right, are there any built in capabilities for
doing so in RQtl or any ideas on how to code it? Thanks in advance.
Fernando

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Hypothesis testing under CIM
parts:
The usual treatment of CIM is to compare the model with cofactors + QTL under test versus just the cofactors, where at any given position the cofactors within some window are excluded from each of the null and alternative. This is what the LOD scores that come from cim() correspond to. To establish significance, one would use a permutation test, including the selection of cofactors as part of the evaluation.

But I would encourage you to focus on the MQM code rather than the cim() function. Even more, I would suggest focusing on the multiple-QTL model functions fitqtl(), addqtl(), stepwiseqtl(), etc.

Evaluating evidence for individual QTL in the context of a multiple-QTL model is not easy and should not be reduced to a series of hypothesis tests.

karl

Dear Karl,
Thank you for your reply and your feedback. I wrote a function to do
the hypothesis testing exactly as you described. I will explore the
multiple-QTL models.

I have a "naive" question that is somehow related to this one. Could
you please explain how do the following functions get the QTL effects?
1. fitqtl with the option get.ests=T and, 2. effectscan
How do these functions know where to get the effects from, i.e. model
behind? They seem to give the same results. I read as much as possible
the documentation, but I couldn't figure it out.
Thanks in advance for your reply.
Fernando

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: Hypothesis testing under CIM
parts:
fitqtl will either use imputation or Haley-Knott regression (depending on method="imp" or method="hk").

effectscan exclusively uses imputation.

karl
